events.summary: India commenced capacity-building programme for 40 Sri Lankan civil servants.
Cabinet approved Japan’s grant for health upgrades at BIA and Colombo Port.
Epilepsy Hospital and Health Centres project was declared open in December 2017.
Cabinet approved a fund and government donation for children affected by Gaza violence.
CEB submitted a proposal to reduce electricity tariffs.
Cabinet approved extending the National Mine Action Centre through 2027.
MoUs were signed to facilitate international aid-based programmes in Northern and Eastern provinces.
Cabinet approved allocating six-acre land for an Indian-assisted monastery.
Two IMF EFF tranches totaling US$670 million had been disbursed.
India-funded hybrid renewable energy systems were being implemented across three Jaffna islands.
Sri Lanka established its Data Protection Authority under a July 2023 gazette.
Cabinet approved tax reductions and free baggage allowance for Sri Lanka–India ferry travel.
India launched construction of 1,300 houses across 45 estates in 10 districts.
Japan signed a grant agreement to install solar facilities at three hospitals.
CEB proposed a new electricity tariff revision, including a three percent decrease.
India’s UPI officially launched in Sri Lanka through a LankaPay partnership.
Construction of Katunayake Airport second terminal stopped in 2022.
Second terminal construction began under a Rs. 145 billion JICA loan.
JICA said it would support resuming Katunayake Airport second-terminal construction.
Construction work continued, with six percent of the terminal completed.
ADB pledged US$8 million for smart agriculture in Mahaweli zones.
JICA pledged a grant for renewable energy units at Sri Lankan hospitals.
JICA completed the Safe Water Supply Project in Anuradhapura.
Sri Lanka requested continued JICA assistance for CEB reforms.
JICA assisted CEB reform-secretariat setup with finance, technical support and experts.
Sri Lankan delegation began India capacity-building visit
Sri Lanka signed agreement supporting Ramayana Trail development
Cabinet approved housing programme offering migrant workers loans
India launched capacity-building programme for Sri Lankan senior civil servants.
India’s UPI payment services launched in Sri Lanka through LankaPay.
UPI transactions via LankaQR officially launched for Indian tourists.
India announced UPI services would launch in Sri Lanka on February 12.
India’s UPI payment gateway was scheduled for launch on February 12.
India and Sri Lanka discussed a proposed multi-product petroleum pipeline.
Cabinet approved importing up to 15,000 tons of cashew nuts.
Rividhanavi was awarded the Siyambalanduwa solar project by end-2023.
CEB and Rividhanavi signed a power purchase agreement for 100MW solar.
Estimated total investment was reduced to US$133 million.
Cabinet approved cannabis cultivation and allied-product manufacture solely for export.
Cabinet approved importing up to 15,000 tonnes of cashews this year.
Cabinet cleared the National Disaster Management Plan for Parliament approval.
Japan pledged funding for solar systems at three Sri Lankan hospitals.
Sri Lanka allocated Rs10 billion for presidential and general elections in 2024.
Government plans to restart suspended highway projects after debt restructuring.
Government plans to restart the suspended airport expansion near Colombo.
Sri Lanka plans to restart a suspended Japan-backed light railway project.
Cabinet approved medicinal cannabis cultivation and export arrangements.
Sri Lanka and World Bank signed financing agreement for financial-sector safety-net strengthening.
Government and World Bank signed financing agreement for financial-sector safety-net strengthening.
Cabinet approved revised Aswesuma implementation and expanded vulnerable-family coverage.
India provided an advance for Sri Lanka’s digital Unique ID project.
Sri Lanka called fresh tenders after previous Unique ID project bids failed.
Cabinet approved separating SLIC life and general insurance businesses.
Cabinet approved transferring SLIC businesses to wholly owned subsidiaries.
Australia and Sri Lanka signed a governance-strengthening arrangement funded over five years.
